result:
**lane.statusfresh is done.** PR #150 ready, `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`, all three CI checks green at head `92f77cacf5`, unlabelled so the board routes it to `needs-audit-1` on its next tick.

**The fix.** GitHub renders a comment's `created_at`, never its `updated_at`, and never moves an edited comment — so #107's in-place PATCH showed `02:28Z` over a body written at `13:32Z`. The clock now goes where GitHub surfaces it: the **issue body** (a short header — minute, counts, deadline, comment link, and the warning about that timestamp) and the **issue title** (clock quantised to the timer's period, plus the lane/arm counts, re-sent only when the string changes). The page also states its own deadline every render and reports a lapse of more than two floors once it has ended. The comment, its id, the create-if-missing fallback, and everything the page reports are unchanged.

**The design was measured, not assumed** — against PR #150 itself: a title PATCH with a new string appends a permanent `renamed` row, the same string appends nothing, a body PATCH makes no timeline event. With `subscribers_count: 0` and `status.sh` authenticating as the owner, renaming notifies nobody; the quantisation is about timeline litter on the page being fixed, not notifications.

**Two defects found on the way**, both fixed: `gh issue list --jq '.[0].number'` yields the string `"null"` on an empty list, which the old empty-check missed, sending every later call to `PATCH /issues/null` — returning 0 while the page went nowhere; and the now-reachable create path is gated on the query having succeeded so a blip can't fork the status issue.

**Verification:** `selftest: 340 passed, 0 failed` with `== status.sh freshness` in the CI log; 27/27 on this branch and 21/27 failing against `415dcc6997`, across body, title and lapse rather than one cause repeated. `preflight.sh` passes including the territory and board-files gates.

Two things I want to flag rather than bury, both in `NOTES.md` and the PR body:

- `docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN.md` still calls the roll-up "rewriting one comment" (§168, §734). That's now incomplete. I left it — it isn't this lane's file and many lanes touch it — so it needs folding into whichever lane owns that path next.
- The *current*-silence hole is not closed and can't be from inside this script: a roll-up that isn't running writes nothing. Closing it properly needs a writer that isn't the host, e.g. a scheduled Actions run that marks the page stale when the host goes quiet. That's a candidate for a follow-up brief if you want it.

One process note on my own work: my first CI watcher reported "settled" while both builds were still running, because its terminal condition matched `COMPLETED` anywhere in the joined string — one green check satisfied it. I caught it, rewrote the condition to require no check pending, and the result above is from the corrected watcher.
